First, in the first 1.9 seconds, Barnaby, seated at the base of the hollow as in the first frame, gets up briskly: at about second 0.4 he braces his own right forearm against the amber wall right at the golden sap drip to push himself up, so the small orange-red maple leaf from the drip and a smear of golden sap stay stuck on the red knitted sleeve of his right forearm, and the drip is left on the wall without its leaf; by about second 1.1 he stands upright on his two hind legs like a person with Hazel still on his shoulder holding her nut, and at about second 1.3 he rubs his clean nose once with the inside of his left sleeve; his nose and face are clean, and the leaf and the golden smear stay on his right sleeve in the same place for the rest of the clip. Then, at about second 2.0, he closes his eyes, lifts his chin and speaks to his own nose, 'Nose, I know you love pie. But today, please... find Mama.' After that, from about second 4.9, there is a silence of one and a half seconds: out of the moonlit fog to the right of the picture a thin cream-gold scent ribbon drifts back and curls up to his nose, his ears swing forward and at about second 6.1 he opens his eyes. At about second 6.4 he says, pointing along the ribbon to the right with one hoof, 'Warm wool. Mama's shawl! This way!' At about second 8.2 Hazel asks, her head tilted, 'Not pie?' and at about second 9.1 Barnaby answers firmly, 'Not pie. Mama.' At about second 10.2 Hazel points ahead to the right and says, 'Go.' and at about second 10.8 Barnaby, already standing upright, sets off at a quick walk toward the right edge and is out of the frame at the right edge by about second 11.8. His antlers stay on his head the whole time. He keeps his back straight and tall with only his head tipped forward when he sniffs and never drops onto four legs.

SCENE: a huge old maple hollow at night exactly as in the first frame, the open hollow mouth; the night sky starts with the thin pale veil of cloud from the first frame, drifting slowly toward the picture-right in a faint breeze with the fallen red leaves stirring the same way, and no moon visible, and at about second 0.6 the veil, still drifting on in the same breeze toward the picture-right, slides off and uncovers the full moon, already there behind the cloud from the very first moment, above a silver-violet fog, so that the moonlight then falls inside the hollow mouth and faces are clearly readable, the night is a deep blue and never black, a soft steady warm amber glow inside the hollow exactly as in the first frame, with cool silver moonlight on the outside and on the edges of their fur, no snow. On the amber wall at the picture-right of the hollow, one golden sap drip with one small orange-red maple leaf stuck to its lower end is already there from the very first moment, until Barnaby's forearm takes the leaf. The thin cream-gold scent ribbon is not there at the start and returns from the right at about second 4.9.

CAMERA: Shot 1: a locked-off medium wide shot inside the hollow mouth, the same size and framing as the first frame, wide enough that Barnaby's whole figure standing upright stays inside the frame, single continuous take, no cut, no zoom, no reframe, the camera does not move at all, only the characters move, also as he leaves toward the right edge of the frame; his whole antlers stay inside the frame with open space above them. Barnaby's full antlers stay inside the frame with clear headroom above them the whole shot. Barnaby's full antlers stay inside the frame with at least 15 percent of the frame height as open space above the antler tips, also at the moment he stands up straight.

SOUND: only natural on-set sounds: a faint unvoiced breeze over the open valley, a dry, quiet, unpitched air inside the hollow, from 0.0 s to 1.9 s a soft sweater rustle as he rises, at 0.5 s one soft pat of his forearm on the wall, at 1.3 s a soft knit-sleeve brush against his nose, at 5.3 s one deep relaxed breath through his nose of 0.6 s, at 6.1 s one tiny soft catch of breath as his eyes open, a soft rustle of dry leaves, from 10.8 s soft footsteps on dry leaves, a very short soft unpitched room tail after each line, each word heard once, Barnaby's voice a warm low rounded young male voice and Hazel's voice a tiny high bright light girl chipmunk voice, clearly higher and lighter than his, saying their lines one at a time, never together.
